title: What is topical authority in SEO? A forward-looking guide for 2027
summary: Topical authority in SEO, updated for AI search: define it, pick the right topics, measure your share against competitors, and track progress.
body_markdown:
A buyer researching email deliverability asks Google why emails land in spam, then asks ChatGPT how to improve their sender reputation, and checks Reddit for tools others have paid for. That whole journey is where topical authority plays out.


Each search can turn up different brands. In[Semrush’s study of 50,000 brands in ChatGPT](https://www.semrush.com/blog/chatgpt-topic-authority-study/) , related prompts often returned completely different names. Track one prompt, and you look like you’re winning. But look across the topic, and the picture changes.


How strongly do search engines and AI tools connect your brand with the topics you want to be known for? And do they connect your competitors with them more often? That’s what we’re trying to understand with topical authority.


The idea itself isn’t new. For years, deep coverage, topic clusters, and internal links have been standard practices. And they still work. But what's changed is *where* the signals come from and how they get measured.


This guide explains how to build topical authority in LLMs and Google search, choose topics worth your investment, and track whether your results show up in your business’s numbers.


## What is topical authority?


Topical authority is how strongly search engines and AI systems associate a brand with a specific topic compared with its competitors. The association builds through the brand’s own website and mentions elsewhere, including reviews, publications, and communities.


As[Amanda Milligan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amandamilligan/) , Content and Growth Manager at Semrush,[explains in Search Engine Land](https://searchengineland.com/guide/topical-authority-for-ai-search) :


> “The phrase ‘topical authority’ has been around for a long time, but the thinking around it has evolved significantly. At its core, it’s always been about your brand becoming associated with specific topics. What’s changed is how we try to build that association.”


The goal of building topical authority is to keep your brand visible as buyers transition between Google and AI tools, from researching a problem to selecting a solution.


There’s room to compete, too. Semrush’s 50,000-brand study found that 53.7% of the ChatGPT categories analyzed had no brand appearing in at least three of five related prompts. Focus on a topic related to your product and address the questions that buyers have before purchasing.


### What counts as a topic?


A topic is a group of related keywords and AI prompts about one subject. For example, “email deliverability” is a topic. And it includes Google searches like “why are my emails going to spam,” and ChatGPT prompts like “how do I improve my sender reputation after a cold outreach campaign?”


The questions cover different parts of the same problem. But to assess topical authority, we look at how consistently a brand appears across the group and how it’s described.


A brand can be strongly associated with one subject and barely appear in searches about a related one.


Take Email on Acid, a pre-send email testing tool (now part of Mailgun Inspect). In the October 2026 Google AI Overview for “best email deliverability tools,” Google listed it under “inbox placement and spam testing,” for checking how emails display before sending.


That’s Google. Now ask ChatGPT a related question, “What are the best email testing tools?” Email on Acid appears again, this time for cross-client testing, alongside Litmus for email previews and rendering.


Across the two responses, Email on Acid is associated with pre-send testing within the broader deliverability topic. To assess the strength of that association, we’ll need to repeat the comparison across related questions and track how consistently the brand appears against competitors.


### Why is publishing more not enough to build topical authority?


Publishing more isn’t enough because topical authority depends on visibility across questions, not the number of pages published. In[Semrush’s topical focus study](https://www.semrush.com/blog/chatgpt-topical-focus-study/) , brands that appeared in only one of a category’s five representative prompts were associated with a lower share of brand mentions. In the sample, the negative association disappeared when a brand appeared in at least three.


More pages can also work against you. Pages that repeat the same advice compete with each other and leave other parts of the topic unanswered.


## How does AI search change topical authority? And what remains the same?


Google’s[guidance for AI Overviews and AI Mode](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) confirms that established SEO practices still apply. Your pages need to be accessible, eligible to appear in search, and helpful to readers. There’s no separate set of technical requirements for appearing in Google’s AI features.


The work on your website still counts. Covering a subject thoroughly, organizing those answers into[topic clusters](https://www.semrush.com/blog/topic-clusters/) , and connecting related pages with[internal links](https://www.semrush.com/blog/internal-links/) all still help readers and search engines find what they need.


What’s changed is how an AI system can research a question, and which sources it draws on to answer it.


### What is topical authority in LLMs?


Topical authority in LLMs is how strongly an AI system associates a brand with a subject compared with competing brands. When the system searches the web to answer a question, it can draw on the brand’s own content and what other sources say about it.


AI Overviews and AI Mode may use what Google calls[query fan-out](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) : running several related searches across subtopics and sources to build a single response.


For the prompt “What are the best email testing tools?” that could mean separate searches for tools that preview emails across clients, check links, flag accessibility issues, and assess spam risk.


[Query fan-out](https://www.semrush.com/blog/query-fan-out/) is also one of the reasons why one keyword ranking can’t tell us how visible a brand is across AI answers. A single response can draw on several searches, and a brand may appear in some of them and not others.


### Your brand’s association with a topic extends beyond your website


In Google search, on-site coverage and backlinks have long helped establish a site’s authority on a topic. Now, assessing the same association across search and AI means looking at a wider set of signals: search rankings, AI citations, industry publications, community threads, social posts, earned media, and how often people search for the brand by name.


In Semrush’s 50,000-brand study, branded search volume was the only domain-level metric that consistently aligned with topic leadership, and even then the edge was modest.


### Different topics draw on different sources


AI systems don’t rely on the same sources for every subject. In[Kevin Indig and Amanda Johnson’s research](https://www.growth-memo.com/p/topics-matter-for-third-party-authority) , competitor websites accounted for 33.5% of AI citations for invoicing questions, compared with 7% for questions about starting a business. The analysis used a small client sample, but it shows how the source mix can change with the subject.


The results also vary by industry. In[Semrush’s topical focus study](https://www.semrush.com/blog/chatgpt-topical-focus-study/) , conducted with Kevin, appearing across more of a topic’s prompts was associated with stronger citation share in finance and real estate. In legal and healthcare, even appearing across all five prompts didn’t reliably translate into stronger brand-mention share.


For Email on Acid, that means investigating the publications and communities AI systems draw on for email testing specifically.


## Topical authority vs. domain authority: What’s the difference?


Topical authority is the association between a brand and a specific subject, while domain authority describes the overall strength of a website, estimated largely from its[backlink profile](https://www.semrush.com/blog/what-are-backlinks/) . Semrush assesses domain strength through[Authority Score](https://www.semrush.com/blog/semrush-authority-score-explained/) , which combines link power, organic traffic, and spam signals into one number for the whole domain. The Authority Score helps you compare websites, but it doesn’t establish which subjects a brand leads.


Each addresses a different question:


- Authority Score answers “How strong is this site?”
- Topical authority answers “For this topic, which brand is strongly associated with it, and how does it compare with the alternatives?”


You can see the gap between the two on Email on Acid’s domain.


The domain has an Authority Score of 38 and nearly 7,000 referring domains. Those figures are sitewide. They don’t show that the brand appeared in Google’s AI Overview for pre-send testing but was second in ChatGPT’s list of recommendations.


According to Semrush’s 50,000-brand study, when comparing the brand that led each ChatGPT topic with the runner-up, the leader had a higher Authority Score in 52.5% of pairs and more organic traffic in 48.4%. However, neither metric consistently identified the topic leader.


A high Authority Score suggests a site can compete, but it doesn’t show where. The topic has to be evaluated on its own. Topical authority works alongside backlinks and overall site quality; it doesn’t replace them.


## 1. Choose the topics according to your buyers’ journey


Start with a few topics your customers research and your business can explain from experience. In trying to build authority across everything you do, you cover more ground but don’t give buyers a stronger reason to remember you. A narrower topic can make it easier to build complete coverage around a problem your team understands.


In Semrush’s topical focus study, a brand could appear once in 20 categories and lead none of them. The share of brand mentions increased when a brand appeared consistently across prompts within a category. A scattershot appearance across several categories wasn’t associated with the same gain. If you want an AI answer to name your brand, start with what you’re already known for.


For Email on Acid, that could mean earning repeated mentions for Outlook rendering and dark-mode testing questions.


This is the define stage of[Semrush’s Topical Gravity framework](https://www.semrush.com/blog/topical-gravity/) : decide which topics your brand needs to be associated with.


### Start with what you sell


Start with your products and work outward to the problems buyers need to solve:


- **Products and features** : What does the product help people check, fix, or improve?
- **Use cases** : When does someone need that help?
- **Pre-purchase questions** : What do buyers ask before choosing a tool?


For Email on Acid, that starting list could include email rendering, pre-send testing, and troubleshooting display problems.


Group related questions into candidate topics. Then evaluate each against audience demand, your expertise, and relevance to business goals.


You can also build your starting list from subjects already bringing people to your site. In[Organic Rankings](https://www.semrush.com/analytics/organic/) , enter your domain and open the “ **Topics** ” tab.


Email on Acid’s report groups its ranking pages into topics such as email coding and development, email design and templates, and email deliverability. Review these groups for subjects that connect to your product, then inspect the pages within them.


For example, 822 of the 857 estimated visits in the “Email Security and Spam Avoidance” group come from a page about when email was created. Those visitors aren’t necessarily looking for a testing tool.


Use the report to find candidates, then use[Prompt Research](https://www.semrush.com/ai-seo/prompt-research/) to explore the questions buyers ask AI tools about each topic.


### Check AI demand and competition


Open[Prompt Research](https://www.semrush.com/ai-seo/prompt-research/) in[Semrush’s AI Visibility Toolkit](https://www.semrush.com/lp/ai-toolkit/en/) , enter your domain, and select your target country and AI platforms. In the “ **Topics** ” tab, compare relevance, AI Volume, and intent.


For Email on Acid, the most relevant topic is “Email Testing and Optimization Tools,” with an estimated 1,000 monthly AI searches. “Email Services and Providers” carries nearly 20 times the volume at medium relevance.


It’s tempting to chase the larger number. But look at the summary bar. The top brands mentioned across the domain’s topic space are Gmail, Google, and Yahoo, and the top sources are google.com, youtube.com, and microsoft.com. A brand competing for “email services” is competing with the mailbox providers themselves.


### Invest by channel


Check which sources appear in answers about your priority topic before deciding where to invest. In Prompt Research, switch to the “ **Prompts** ” view to inspect the answers, competing brands, and cited sources.


For example, the comparison prompt “How does Email on Acid compare to other email testing tools?” shows which alternatives appear alongside the brand and how the answer describes it. That’s the positioning Email on Acid may need to reinforce or correct.


Open the prompt with “ **View full response** ,” then examine the “ **Sources** ” panel. The ChatGPT response lists nine sources: four Email on Acid pages, three Litmus pages, and two GlockApps pages. They include pricing, product information, testing guides, and Litmus’s own comparison with Email on Acid.


A buyer asking about Email on Acid can receive an answer partly informed by what Litmus says about it.


The investment follows the sources:


- For “How does Email on Acid compare to other email testing tools?” the team would prioritize an on-site comparison page
- For “What are the best email testing tools?” check the answer’s cited sources to identify relevant publishers to approach
- For “best email deliverability tools,” look at video and editorial lists


### Expand into closely related topics


Once your brand appears consistently across a topic’s related questions, expand into an adjacent subject the same buyer needs help with. Semrush’s topical focus study found that named brand mentions were more common in categories close to a brand’s existing expertise.


Prioritize topics that sit on the buyer journey. Someone asking why an email looks broken in Outlook may next ask how to test it, then which testing tool to buy. Use those connected questions to guide your next topic.


## 2. Measure where you stand against competitors


Topical authority is relative. The question is how often your brand appears compared with the brands a buyer would consider instead, across the keywords and prompts that make up the topic. A single ranking can’t answer it, but a representative set can.


This is the measure stage of Topical Gravity: take each priority topic, choose queries that represent it, and compare every competitor against the same set.


### Set up a simple topic scorecard


To set up a topic scorecard, select five to 10 Google keywords and five to 10 AI prompts for each priority topic. Include questions that cover definitions, practical problems, comparisons, alternatives, and buying decisions.


For email testing, the keywords and prompts could include “what is email rendering,” “how to test emails in Outlook,” and “best email testing tools.”


Record the following for your brand and each competitor, using the same country and date. Keep AI results separate by platform:


**Measure**


**What to record**


Google rankings


Each keyword’s position and the percentage of selected keywords ranking in the top 10


AI mentions


The percentage of sampled answers that name the brand


AI citations


The percentage of sampled answers that cite the domain


For example, if Email on Acid appeared in two of five ChatGPT answers and one of its top competitors, Litmus, appeared in four, their mention rates would be 40% and 80% in that sample — a gap of 40 percentage points.


Then, Email on Acid would investigate: which questions bring Litmus into the answer and leave Email on Acid out?


Track citations separately from mentions. In Semrush’s 50,000-brand study, the most-cited domain was also the most-mentioned brand in only 20.8% of categories. An AI system can use your content to answer a question without naming your brand as an option.


### Find the gaps with Visibility Overview and Topic Opportunities


To find the gaps, open[Visibility Overview](https://www.semrush.com/kb/1596-visibility-overview-report) in the[AI Visibility Toolkit](https://www.semrush.com/lp/ai-toolkit/en/) and enter your domain. Email on Acid scores 19/100 (“Low”). Mentions are up 2.5%, but citations are down 35.6% and cited pages are down 46.2%. Gemini and AI Mode account for more than 70% of its mentions, so a quick check of ChatGPT alone would miss most of them.


Next, scroll to “Topics & Sources,” open “Topic Opportunities,” select the competitors you want to compare, and click “Analyze.” The report identifies prompts where competitors appear and your brand is missing.


Comparing Email on Acid with Litmus, GlockApps, and Mailtrap, the report surfaces broad topics like “Email Marketing Platforms and Services,” with an estimated AI Volume of 899.2K and two of the three competitors mentioned.


But expand the row, and the questions reveal how broad it is: “mailing platform,” “email design company,” “mailer design software,” and “best mail out program.” Someone choosing a mailbox provider has a different need from someone checking a campaign before sending it, so the volume alone doesn’t make this a priority.


Use “ **Filter by topic** ” to find the subjects you selected earlier, then record where the same competitors repeatedly appear without you.


### Use Keyword Overview to assess individual keywords


To assess individual keywords, enter a keyword and your domain in Semrush’s[Keyword Overview](https://www.semrush.com/analytics/keywordoverview/) to see:


- **Topical Authority** : How relevant the domain’s existing content is to the analyzed keyword
- **Personal Keyword Difficulty** : How difficult Semrush estimates it would be for your domain to rank in Google’s top 10 for that keyword


For “email testing,” Semrush rates Email on Acid’s Topical Authority as “High” and its Personal Keyword Difficulty at 43% (“Possible”). The domain, however, ranks outside the top 100 in US desktop results for this keyword.


Scroll to “SERP Analysis” and select “ **Domain** ” to see who ranks instead. Semrush estimates Email on Acid’s potential position at 81.


Mailgun.com sits in fourth place with its email testing software page. A buyer searching for email testing can already find the product’s new home, even when the old domain is out of view.


The Topical Authority label describes how relevant one domain is to one Google keyword, not its topic-wide AI visibility. Use Keyword Overview to plan specific pages within a topic; use Visibility Overview, Topic Opportunities, and the topic scorecard to assess the brand’s visibility across Google and AI search against named competitors.


## 3. Build authority on a topic


Use the gaps you found in the competitor comparison to decide what to improve and publish. The aim is to give buyers complete answers and give other sources a reason to refer to your brand when discussing the subject.


The build stage has two halves:


- Coverage on your own site
- Mentions on the sources AI systems and search engines consult for your topic


### Create a topical authority map


To create a topical authority map, plan a main overview page, called a[pillar page](https://www.semrush.com/blog/pillar-page) , linked to more detailed pages covering subtopics, specific questions, comparisons, use cases, and buying decisions. The topic is the set of keywords and prompts people use, and the map is how your site answers those questions.


[Keyword Strategy Builder](https://www.semrush.com/analytics/keywordmanager/) can draft a map from a[seed keyword](https://www.semrush.com/blog/seed-keywords/) . For “email testing,” it suggests “test email across clients free” as a pillar page under “email rendering and compatibility testing,” grouping 12 keywords, including “email testing” and “email testing services,” with 10 supporting pages.


Treat the suggestions as a draft. Compare them with your existing pages and the buyer questions you found in[Prompt Research](https://www.semrush.com/ai-seo/prompt-research/) .


Check for overlap before adding pages to the plan. For example, “email preview” and “preview text in email” sound alike, but one is about how an email renders and the other about the preheader line. Review their keywords and search intent before deciding.


Then, plan the internal links. The overview should lead readers to detailed answers, and those pages should connect to the next relevant question.


### Give each page a clear purpose


A topic with good coverage answers different questions within it. For email testing, a reader may need to diagnose a display problem, establish a testing process, or choose between tools. Each task calls for different information.


**Page purpose**


**What to cover**


Explain the topic


What pre-send email testing involves and which problems it can catch


Solve a specific problem


How to diagnose and fix white lines in Outlook emails


Address a use case


How a team can test transactional emails before releasing a new template


Support a buying decision


How testing tools compare on supported clients and pricing


For example, Email on Acid’s blog covers technical articles on Outlook rendering problems, email fonts, dark mode, and HTML table roles. Each addresses a different part of designing and testing an email.


Before commissioning another page, check whether an existing one already serves the same intent. For instance, two articles about Outlook aren’t automatically duplicates. But if both answer the same question with the same advice, combine their strongest material into one page and redirect the other.


### Publish something others can learn from


A clear point of view and original findings make readers remember those who helped them. Google’s[helpful, people-first content guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) also considers whether a page contributes original information or perspectives beyond what other websites provide.


Make the[expertise behind the work](https://www.semrush.com/blog/eeat/) visible. Name the people who ran the tests, explain the method, and show the product details behind the conclusions.


### Earn mentions in sources relevant to the topic


Off-site authority includes backlinks and how other sources describe your brand. Return to the “ **Sources** ” panel in[Prompt Research](https://www.semrush.com/ai-seo/prompt-research/) to identify publications, review sites, and communities cited for your priority questions. Those are places to investigate for relevant coverage, expert contributions, and accurate product information.


- **Industry publications** : Offer original findings or expert commentary that helps explain a problem
- **Review sites** : Keep product information accurate and invite customers to describe their actual use cases in honest reviews
- **Relevant communities** : Answer technical questions with enough detail to help, disclose your connection to the brand, and link to supporting material when appropriate


Email on Acid already has an example of a relevant publisher mention. *CMSWire* ’s article on email measurement credits and links to the brand’s explanation of email engagement, making Email on Acid a named reference in a discussion of how marketers should measure email performance.


AI answers can draw on your own description of the product and what other sources say about it. Entity clarity means making the product’s identity and capabilities explicit across those sources.


For Email on Acid, those descriptions include:


- **Its own channels** : Pre-deployment email QA
- **The ChatGPT comparison** : A rendering and QA tool
- **Litmus’s comparison** : The product presented on a competitor’s terms


[Keep the facts consistent](https://www.semrush.com/blog/brand-positioning-is-an-ai-search-variable/) across your product pages, review profiles, and contributed articles. Correct outdated descriptions where you can, and publish your own comparison with clear evidence and honest trade-offs. You can’t control a competitor’s account of your product, but you can give buyers another source to consult.


For Email on Acid (now part of Mailgun Inspect), a quarter’s work on topical authority could include:


- **An on-site update** : Publish a “Mailgun Inspect (formerly Email on Acid) vs. Litmus” comparison page with a feature table and honest trade-offs, so buyers get the brand’s own account alongside Litmus’s and learn about the rename
- **An original point-of-view piece** : Build on the email-engagement explanation CMSWire referenced, using original testing data to support a clear position on what marketers should measure
- **A third-party mention** : Pitch those findings to relevant email and martech publications identified in the source review, and update the G2 profile so its product description reflects the same capabilities


## 4. Track progress over time


Track the keywords and prompts that make up each priority topic so you can see where your brand’s visibility is growing and where competitors still appear instead.


Use Semrush’s[Position Tracking](https://www.semrush.com/position-tracking/) for Google keywords and[Prompt Tracking](https://www.semrush.com/kb/1503-prompt-tracking) for AI prompts. In both, choose what to track, add competitors, and compare results over time.


### Set up tracking per topic


Group your tracked keywords and prompts by topic so you can review each subject separately.


In[Position Tracking](https://www.semrush.com/position-tracking/) , select “ **Google** ” as the search engine and your target location, then add your topic’s keywords and competitors and group related keywords with a topic tag.


Open “ **Overview** ” to check each keyword’s position and ranking page, then monitor whether the relevant testing pages gain visibility.


The summary for Email on Acid’s 10 tracked keywords shows which ones gained or lost visibility and flags mailgun.com as a potential competitor. But Mailgun Inspect is the product’s successor, so what looks like a competitor gaining ground could be the product’s new home gaining visibility. Track both domains to avoid mistaking that shift for a loss.


In[Prompt Tracking](https://www.semrush.com/kb/1503-prompt-tracking) , click “ **Tag prompts** ” to group related questions under a topic such as “email testing.” Use that group to review the topic’s performance over time.


The “ **Sources** ” report shows which domains and pages appear across the tracked answers.


The report lists 113 cited pages across the tracked responses. The rows include Maizzle, React Email, MJML, and Litmus, with zero recorded brand mentions in the associated answers. That makes this table the shortlist for the off-site work in “Earn mentions in sources relevant to the topic.”


### Keep the prompts consistent, and the questions varied


Keep a core set of prompts unchanged so you can compare results over time. But choose questions that cover different parts of the buyer’s research.


Semrush’s 50,000-brand study used five question types to represent a category:


- A definition
- A comparison
- An alternatives question
- A use case
- A buying question


Use that range as a starting point and add the relevant keyword equivalents in Position Tracking.


Read the results as a set: record a baseline, then compare after a quarter.


If your brand appears in two of five prompts this month and four of five next quarter, the topic is moving, whichever prompt flipped. Then check which questions account for the gain and whether competitors gained too.


Look for changes in:


- **Coverage across the topic** : More relevant keywords reach your chosen Google benchmark, such as the top 10, and more tracked AI prompts name your brand. Report those measures separately.
- **Brand mentions** : Your brand appears repeatedly across different questions and platforms, alongside the citations you’re already tracking
- **Brand positioning** : Read the comparison and buying answers to see how they describe your product. For Email on Acid, that means being associated consistently with pre-send QA and rendering tests.


## Tie topical authority to business outcomes


What do you want your buyers to do? For Email on Acid, “grow trial sign-ups from email testing pages by 20% in two quarters” gives the work a business target.


- Group the pages on each topic’s map in your analytics and track their leads, trials, and conversions
- Follow identifiable AI referrals through to sales opportunities in your CRM
- Watch branded searches, including queries like “email on acid spam test,” which connect the brand to the subject you want it known for


If visibility grows but inquiries don’t, look at where the interest stops:


- Are the pages attracting prospective customers?
- Do they explain how the product solves their problem?


More coverage won’t necessarily fix what’s missing. And topical authority can only account for part of the result. Email on Acid might appear in every relevant comparison and still lose a buyer over price or a missing feature.


## FAQs


### How many articles do you need to build topical authority?


You don’t need a set number of articles to build topical authority. Plan around the questions your audience needs answered, with each page covering a distinct search intent.


### Is topical authority a ranking factor for Google?


Google hasn’t confirmed topical authority as a standalone ranking factor for general search. But it does use a[“topic authority” system](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/05/understanding-news-topic-authority) to surface news from publishers with expertise in a subject or location.


### How long does it take to build topical authority?


Building topical authority takes a sustained effort over months, with no guaranteed deadline.[Google says](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/core-updates) recognizing lasting improvements in content quality can take several months.


### Is topical authority different from domain authority?


Yes, topical authority describes how strongly a brand is associated with a specific subject; domain authority describes broader website strength, often estimated through third-party SEO scores.


### Does topical authority work the same way in AI search?


Topical authority works in a similar way in AI search, but not exactly the same. Google’s AI search uses familiar SEO foundations but can search across related subtopics to assemble answers, so track AI citations separately from rankings.


### Can a new or small site build topical authority?


Yes, a new or small site can build topical authority. Start with a narrow subject you know well, publish original answers, and connect related pages with internal links. Expand as your coverage develops.
